TRANSLATION OF FRENCH DOCUMENT NO. 167/S DATED DECEMBER 14,1936.
（印：SECRET）

Subject: Situation on the Suiyuan-Charhar Frontier.
Reference: Sino-Japanese Relations - National Defence.

It is extremely difficult to give an account of the events
now taking place in Suiyuan without first having some insight
as to the geographical peculiarities of this province, and also
having a retrospective glimpse of the struggles of the Russians,
Chinese and at last the Japanese for this part of Mongolia.

Poor and without natural resources, an undefined succession
of plains where grass rarely is to be seen, this province, where
in winter the cold is intense, has been for all time the centre
of an extensive cattle (pony) breeding ground. To the north,
the desert character of the soil has been a barrier against the
Russian penetration, whilst to the South on the border of Shansi,
the fertility of the valleys has caused an incessant influx of
Chinese colonists, who, farmers by nature, have compelled their
Mongolian counterparts to withdraw towards the north. (The pop-
ulation of Inner Mongolia comprises 12,000,000 inhabitants, of
which 2,500,000 only are Mongolians). It is in the enmity and
antagonism between the nomadic and sedentary tribes that the
source of all the difficulties which have separated the Mongols
and Chinese can be seen.

Even in 1911 the Chinese was considered by the Mongolian as
an enemy and the enmity between the two races at that time was
very bitter; but the arid nature of the soil of the North of
Inner Mongolia had prevented the Russian influence from extending
as far as Ourga with the result that the old social system of the
times of Gengis Khan was still able to exist. Inner Mongolia
guarded its millenial outlook with its feudalism and princes,
its lamas and its monks for whom the greater part of the shepherds
and farmers worked like slaves. The artificial delimitation
of Mongolia into provinces after the proclamation of the Republic
of China did not change the state of these affairs. But in
page_data.zh:
1936年12月14日法国文件第167/S号译文。
（印章：秘密）

主题：绥远-察哈尔边境局势。
参考：中日关系 - 国防。

如果不先了解该省的地理特殊性，并回顾俄罗斯人、中国人以及最后日本人争夺蒙古这一地区的斗争历史，就很难描述目前在绥远发生的事件。

该省贫穷且缺乏自然资源，是一望无际的平原，鲜见青草，冬季严寒，历来是广阔的牲畜（小马）养殖中心。北部，土壤的沙漠特征构成了阻挡俄罗斯渗透的屏障，而南部与山西接壤处，山谷的肥沃吸引了中国殖民者不断涌入，这些天生是农民的人迫使他们的蒙古同行向北撤退。（内蒙古人口包括1200万居民，其中只有250万是蒙古人）。游牧部落与定居部落之间的敌意和对立，正是蒙汉分离所有困难的根源所在。

即使在1911年，蒙古人也将中国人视为敌人，当时两个种族之间的敌意非常激烈；但内蒙古北部土壤的干旱性质阻止了俄罗斯影响力延伸至库伦，结果是成吉思汗时代的旧社会制度得以存续。内蒙古以其封建主义和王公、喇嘛和僧侣守护着其千年的面貌，绝大多数牧民和农民像奴隶一样为他们劳作。中华民国成立后将蒙古人为划分为各省，并未改变这种状况。但在

page_data.en:
- 2 -
uniting, under an administration more and more purely Chinese,
those Mongolian plains as territory for Chinese colonisation, the
Chinese Government only accentuated the desire for autonomy of
the Mongols.
From Ourga the liberation movement was launched, and in 1912
Outer Mongolia, with the support of Russia, declared its inde-
pendance. The Mongols of the South, supported by the Ourga
Mongols, declared themselves as being against the Chinese and
requested a Union with Outer Mongolia with the object of forming
a single State. The Russian Government in power after the
Treaty of Portsmouth having recognized Japanese influence in the
Western part of Inner Mongolia, was unable to seriously support
the independance movement of the Mongolians of the South and
in 1916 this embryo separatist movement was crushed by YUAN SHIH
KAI. After the sovietisation of Outer Mongolia in 1923-4,
fearing for their privileges, the Mongol princes and clergy
turned towards China and joined themselves to this country. Thus
is explained the reason why Russian expansion has progessed no
further, the rapid making and opening of a railway line from
Peiping to Paotow and the complete social order which reigned in
Inner Mongolia up till 1931, when Manchuria was occupied by the
Japanese.
It was no longer the same question after the occupation of
Jehol by Japan and the creation by the Manchukuoan Government of
Mongolian autonomous districts. Measures taken by the Japanese
to extend their influence among the Mongols of the South provoked
many hot-brained ■■■ sporadic movements. In the first half of
September, 1933, a conference of Mongolian princes took place at
Pailingmiao under the preidency of Prince TEH WANG (德 王 );
who was at this time, a member of the Charhar provincial Government.
At the termination of the conference, a telegram requesting the
creation of an autonomous regime for Inner Mongolia was despatched
to the Nanking Government. Although this telegram clearly stated
the loyalty of the signatories towards the Nanking Government, the
government saw - not without reason however - the menace of a
page_data.zh:
- 2 -
将这些蒙古平原作为中国人殖民地在日益纯粹的中国行政管理下统一起来时，中国政府只是加剧了蒙古人的自治愿望。
解放运动从库伦发起，1912年，在外蒙古在俄罗斯的支持下宣布独立。南部的蒙古人在库伦蒙古人的支持下，宣布反对中国人，并要求与外蒙古联合，目的是形成一个单一的国家。《朴茨茅斯条约》后掌权的俄罗斯政府承认了日本在内蒙古西部的影响力，因此无法认真支持南部蒙古人的独立运动，1916年，这一胚胎般的分离主义运动被袁世凯镇压。1923-4年外蒙古苏维埃化后，蒙古王公和神职人员担心自己的特权，转向中国并与该国结盟。这就解释了为什么俄罗斯的扩张没有进一步深入，北京至包头铁路线的快速修建和开通，以及直到1931年日本占领满洲之前内蒙古享有的完全社会秩序。
在日本占领热河以及满洲国政府建立蒙古自治区之后，情况就不再一样了。日本人为扩大其在南部蒙古人中的影响力所采取的措施引发了许多热血 ■■■ 零星运动。1933年9月上半月，蒙古王公会议在百灵庙召开，由德王（时任察哈尔省政府成员）主持。会议结束时，向南京政府发送了一份请求为内蒙古建立自治政权的电报。虽然这份电报明确陈述了签署人对南京政府的忠诚，但政府并非毫无理由地看到了……的威胁

page_data.en:
- 3 -
separatist movement fomented by Japanese agents. In order to
thwart thos movement, Nanking created in 1934 (March) a "Political
Commission for Mongolian Autonomy," a type of Mongolian autonomous
government. The headquarters were at Pailingmiao and it was was
placed under the presidency of Prince YUN, chief of the Ulantsab
tribe.
With the formation of this commission, it became quite evident
that the principal role was being played, not by the president, but
by the Secretary-General of the Commission, Prince TEH WANG. Having
pro-Japanese tendencies - he studied in Japan - Prince TEH easily
fell under the influence of Japanese agents who promised him their
moral and financial support. In April, and May 1935 Prince TEH
made several trips to Hsinking. According to the terms of an
agreement drawn up at that time between the Prince and the Govern-
ment of Manchukuo, assistance was promised the Prince for the
organisation of a Mongolian army along modern lines, and the
creation of an independant Mongolian state, allied to Manchukuo,
and of which he would become the supreme head.
In order to realise these projects, it was necessary at first
to lessen the authority of General CHANG CHIH CHUNG (張自忠),
president at this time of the Charhar Provincial Government, who
had tried by all means to limit the carrying of the autonomy
agreed to in March 1934. The occupation in May and June, 1935
by Japanese garrisons, of Dolonor and other strategic points in
Charhar, compelled General CHANG to take a stand against the
Japanese. Following protests from the Japanese, the Central
Government disowned him, and the HO YING CHING - UMETSU (何应钦—梅津)
Agreement acknowledged the new Japanese conquest.
For several months, the terms of this verbal agreement
were interpreted and distorted by the Japanese to permit them
to justify their successive encroachments and those of Prince
TEH. In order to end the growing influence of the Prince,
the Chinese Government decided to finish with him. It decided
on January 25, 1935 to divide those territories administered
for nearly two years by the Political Commission of Inner
page_data.zh:
- 3 -
由日本特务煽动的分离主义运动。为了挫败这一运动，南京政府于1934年（3月）成立了“蒙古自治政务委员会”，这是一种蒙古自治政府形式。总部设在百灵庙，由乌兰察布盟盟长云王（Prince YUN）担任委员长。

随着该委员会的成立，很明显，发挥主要作用的并非委员长，而是委员会秘书长德王（Prince TEH WANG）。德王具有亲日倾向——他曾留学日本——因此很容易受到日本特务的影响，这些特务向他承诺提供道义和财政支持。1935年4月和5月，德王数次前往新京。根据当时德王与满洲国政府之间拟定的一项协议条款，对方承诺协助德王按现代方式组建蒙古军队，并建立一个与满洲国结盟的独立蒙古国家，由他担任最高元首。

为了实现这些计划，首先必须削弱时任察哈尔省政府主席张自忠将军（General CHANG CHIH CHUNG）的权威，他一直试图通过各种手段限制1934年3月商定的自治权的实施。1935年5月和6月，日本驻军占领了多伦诺尔及察哈尔的其他战略要点，迫使张将军采取对日立场。在日本提出抗议后，中央政府与他划清界限，而《何应钦—梅津协定》（HO YING CHING - UMETSU Agreement）则承认了日本的新征服成果。

数月间，日本人曲解和歪曲这项口头协定的条款，以证明其 successive encroachments（连续侵蚀）以及德王的行动是正当的。为了结束德王日益增长的影响力，中国政府决定彻底解决他的问题。1935年1月25日，中国政府决定分割由内蒙古政治委员会管理了近两年的那些领土，

page_data.en:
- 4 -
Mongolia, and placed Western Suiyuan under the direction of a
new Commission which took the name of the Autonomous Political
Commission of the banners and leagues of Suiyuan. Prince SHA
(沙王) was named President and General YEN HSI SHAN (錫山)
"protector." Although the headquarters of Prince TEH remain
at Pailingmiao (Suiyuan), the creation of this organ has limited
the activities of Prince Teh in Mongolian affairs in Charhar.

Defence measures taken by the Nanking Government have pre-
expansion
vented the "peaceful" ^ of Japanese influence on all of Inner Mon-
golia and they have obliged the Japanese to envisage the mainten-
ance of measures of a political nature already taken by military
operations. Without running the risk of being accused of exag-
geration, one can state that the occupation of Suiyuan has been
considered for a long time by the Japanese or rather by its mili-
tary, as a matter of vital importance. From a strategic point of
view, the transformation of Suiyuan into a part of Manchukuo
would have for the Japanese the advantage of cutting all lines of
communication between Shansi and Soviet Mongolia and the creation
of an independant Mongol State is not realisable without the
inclusion of Suiyuan in the territory of the new State.

In order not to aggravate the present Sino-Japanese
situation, as an aggressor, the Japanese Staff-Major appears
to have wanted to realise the conquest of Suiyuan by the use of
auxiliary forces - of followers. Towards the end of 1935, he
commenced the reorganisation of the Mongol Army of Teh Wang and
the creation of other detachments of Manchu-Mongol troops. At
the beginning of the year Prince Teh was almost in open rebellion
against the Chinese Government. The creation of the Autonomous
Political Commission of the Banners and Leagues of Suiyuan
could only increase his grudge and ill-will. The mutiny on
February 21 of a thousand members of the Peace Preservation Corps
at Pailingmiao, paid by the agents of General FU TSO YI (傅作義)
and the transformation by Nanking on July 21 of the Autonomous
Political Commission of Inner Mongolia into the Political Commission
page_data.zh:
- 4 -
并将绥远西部置于一个新设委员会的管理之下，该委员会命名为“绥远各盟旗自治政务委员会”。沙王（Prince SHA）被任命为委员长，阎锡山将军（General YEN HSI SHAN）任“保护人”。尽管德王的总部仍留在绥远的百灵庙，但该机构的成立限制了德王在察哈尔蒙古事务中的活动。

南京政府采取的防御措施阻止了日本势力对整个内蒙古的“和平”扩张，并迫使日本人考虑维持已通过军事行动采取的政治性质措施。毫不夸张地说，占领绥远长期以来被日本人，或者更确切地说是其军方，视为至关重要之事。从战略角度来看，将绥远变为满洲国的一部分，将使日本切断山西与苏属蒙古之间所有交通线；若不将绥远纳入新国家的领土，建立独立的蒙古国家便无法实现。

为了不加剧当前的中日局势并以侵略者面目出现，日本参谋本部似乎希望通过使用辅助部队——即追随者——来实现对绥远的征服。1935年底，他开始重组德王的蒙古军，并创建其他满蒙部队分队。年初时，德王几乎处于公开反叛中国政府的状态。绥远各盟旗自治政务委员会的成立只能增加他的怨恨和敌意。2月21日，百灵庙一千名保安队成员发生兵变，这些人受傅作义将军（General FU TSO YI）的特务收买；7月21日，南京将内蒙古自治政务委员会改组为察哈尔

page_data.en:
- 5 -
of the Mongolian Leagues and Banners of Charhar must have upset
him even more and compelled him to define his attitude. Further,
the Japanese were able to profit from the losses of cattle
caused by the rigorous winter of 1935-6 and were able to attach
to themselves the Mongolian princes whilst making advances to
them - advances which the Chinese News Agency Kuomin has esti-
mated at fifty millions of yen. The organisation of the "aux-
iliary" forces was finished in August 1936, when the Kwantung
Army Headquarters sent them into action.
At this time - towards the end of September 1936 - the
allied Manchukuo-Mongolian forces comprised:-
1) 1st. Group ; Some 10,000 badly equipped Mongolian cavalry
troops of Prince Teh Wang, having their Headquarters at the
Chapssu Monastery to the north of Pailingmiao.
2) 2nd. Group ; General LI SHOU HSIN's (李守信 ) self-styled
Manchukuo-Mongolian "irregulars". In actual fact, this
group was formed from the 3rd. Infantry Division and the
3rd. Independent Cavalry Brigade of the Manchukuo Army.
Its strength was about 15,000 men and its headquarters was
located at Shangtu.
3) 3rd. Group ; Troops composed of bandits of General WANG
YING (王英 ), who called themselves the "anti-commun-
ist autonomous army." They were about ten to 15 thousand
strong (infantry and cavalry). Their headquarters was at
Changpei.
(The troops of TEH WANG and General LI SHOU HSIN have
Japanese advisers and instructors. As for WANG YING's men, they
have no Japanese instructors, but one adviser, Colonel TANAKA.)
TEH WANG's group was supported by five Manchukuoan
cavalry brigades (the 2nd, 3rd, 4th, 7th and 8th brigades), which
are regular Manchukuoan units organised in 1932 by the Japanese.
These brigades which were stationed along the Manchukuo-Mongolian
frontier, were in May-July, 1936, transferred to Charhar, where
they were concentrated, it appears, in the Taerham-Seyutzewang
regions. Their strength was about eight to ten thousand men.
page_data.zh:
- 5 -
蒙古各盟旗政务委员会，这一定使他更加不安，并迫使他表明态度。此外，日本人利用1935-36年严冬造成的牲畜损失，通过向蒙古王公提供预付款——据中国新闻社国民通讯社估计达五千万日元——将他们拉拢到自己一边。“辅助”部队的组建于1936年8月完成，随后关东军司令部将其投入行动。

此时——即1936年9月底——满蒙联军包括：
1) 第一集团：约10,000名装备不良的德王蒙古骑兵部队，总部设在百灵庙以北的查干苏布尔嘎庙（Chapssu Monastery）。
2) 第二集团：李守信将军（General LI SHOU HSIN）自称的满蒙“杂牌军”。实际上，该集团由满洲国军第三步兵师和第三独立骑兵旅组成。兵力约为15,000人，总部设在上都。
3) 第三集团：由王英将军（General WANG YING）的土匪组成的部队，自称为“防共自治军”。兵力约为一万至一万五千人（步兵和骑兵）。总部设在张北。
（德王和李守信将军的部队配有日本顾问和教官。至于王英的部下，没有日本教官，但有一名顾问，即田中上校（Colonel TANAKA）。）

德王集团得到五个满洲国骑兵旅（第2、3、4、7和8旅）的支持，这些是日本人于1932年组建的满洲国正规部队。这些旅团驻扎在满蒙边境，于1936年5月至7月调往察哈尔，据称集中在达尔罕-四子王旗地区。兵力约为八千至一万人。

page_data.en:
- 6 -

The total strength of the Manchukuo-Mongolian troops
prepared to take part in the Suiyuan operations was approxi-
mately 50,000 men. Of these men, the group of General LI SHOU
HSIN and the regular Manchukuo brigades were well eqipped
and possessed modern arms and accoutrements : automatic rifles,
machine-guns, trench mortars, artillery, tanks and aeroplanes.
All the technical units (aviation and tank units) were placed
under the direct command of Japanese officers and had a mixed
staff - Japanese-Manchukuo and Japanese-Mongolian.

From the Chinese side, the defence of Suiyuan, prior to
October 1, 1936, was solely in the hands of the troops of Gener-
al FU TSO YI (35th. Army), who comprised one division of infantry
(73rd) and two divisions and one brigade of cavalry - altogether
about 18,000 men. The concentration of Manchukuo-Mongolian
troops on the Suiyuan-Chahar frontier compelled General CHIANG
KAI SHEK to reinforce the defence of this province. During
October the 70th, 71st and 72nd. divisions and one division of
cavalry were transferred from Shansi. Another division of
cavalry (2nd) was transferred from Shansi.

In November, these troops were further stengthened by
one division from Shansi (58th), by six divisions (4th. 15th.
41st., 68th., 89th and 99th) and one independant brigade (33rd)
of the Central Government forces, by one division of cavalry
(7th) and by three squadrons of aeroplanes (27 machines), which
brought the strength of the troops stationed at Suiyuan to 10
divisions of infantry, 1 brigade of cavalry, 1 independant bri-
gade, 3 squadrons of aeroplanes, 5 divisions of cavalry - a
total of about 120,000 men.

In addition, during November, a strong reserve was
formed at Taiyuan (Capital of Shansi), comprising of two Shansi
divisions (66th. and 67th), of three Central Government divisions,
(21st. 24th. and 79th) and one regiment of artillery - about
50,000 men altogether.

The month of October was marked by certain activities of
page_data.zh:
- 6 -

准备参加绥远作战的满蒙部队总兵力约为50,000人。在这些人员中，李守信将军的集团和满洲国正规旅装备精良，拥有现代武器和装备：自动步枪、机枪、战壕迫击炮、火炮、坦克和飞机。所有技术兵种（航空和坦克部队）均置于日本军官的直接指挥之下，并设有混合参谋部——日满混合及日蒙混合。

从中方来看，1936年10月1日之前，绥远的防务完全由傅作义将军的部队（第35军）负责，该部包括一个步兵师（第73师）和两个骑兵师及一个骑兵旅——总共约18,000人。满蒙部队在绥远-察哈尔边境的集结迫使蒋介石将军加强该省的防御。10月期间，第70、71和72师以及一个骑兵师从山西调来。另一个骑兵师（第2师）也从山西调来。

11月，这些部队进一步得到加强，包括来自山西的一个师（第58师），中央军六个师（第4、15、41、68、89和99师）和一个独立旅（第33旅），一个骑兵师（第7师）以及三个飞行中队（27架飞机），这使得驻守绥远的部队达到10个步兵师、1个骑兵旅、1个独立旅、3个飞行中队、5个骑兵师——总计约120,000人。

此外，11月期间，在太原（山西省会）组建了一支强大的预备队，包括两个山西师（第66和67师）、三个中央军师（第21、24和79师）以及一个炮兵团——总共约50,000人。

10月份的特点是某些

page_data.en:
- 7 -

reconnaissance detachments. Several skirmishes on the Western
Suiyuan frontier took place. After this, the Government forces
deployed in arc like formation from Tichon to Paotow in order to
protect the Peiping-Suiyuan Railway Line. At the end of the
month, the press officially announced that Prince TEH had sent
to General FU TSO YI, the governor of Suiyuan, the following
ultimatum:
1) The return to the jurisdiction of the Chahar Mongolian
Political Commission of the Banners placed under the
control of Suiyuan since January 1935.
2) Abolition of all military works erected by the Suiyuan
authorities to the south of Pailingmiao and the raising
of the economic blockade against Pailingmiao.
3) Return of arms and ammunition belonging to the Pailingmiao
Peace Preservation Corps, which the Suiyuan authorities
had seized when certain elements of the Corps had mut-
inied during the Spring and turned over to the army of
General FU TSO YI.
4) Payment by the Suiyuan authorities of $200,000.00, pre-
viously deducted on the Mongolian taxes, as liquidation
expenses of the "Mongolian Autonomous Political Commission,"
of Pailingmiao, and
5) Punishment of all those implicated and concerned in the
revolt of the Pailingmiao Peace Preservation Corps.
General FU TSO YI refused to consider these demands, as a
result of which Prince TEH received a telegram from Nanking
reproaching him for his open rebellion.
The attack which was expected was launched on November
5. Coming from Shangtu, their base of departure, the Manchukuo-
Mongolian troops marched on Taolin and Hsinho, two strategic
positions covering the Peiping-Suiyuan Railway Line. Contact
with their objects was made on November 11. On November 15,
the invaders made violent attacks on Taolin, but were repulsed.
On November 18 the Chinese troops successfully launched a
page_data.zh:
- 7 -

侦察分队的活动。绥远西部边境发生了几次小规模冲突。此后，政府军呈弧形部署，从集宁到包头，以保护平绥铁路线。月底，媒体正式宣布德王向绥远省主席傅作义将军发出最后通牒，内容如下：
1) 将自1935年1月以来受绥远控制的各旗归还给察哈尔蒙古政治委员会管辖。
2) 废除绥远当局在百灵庙以南修建的所有军事工事，并解除对百灵庙的经济封锁。
3) 归还属于百灵庙保安队的武器弹药，这些武器弹药是春季该队部分成员兵变并投奔傅作义将军部队时被绥远当局没收的。
4) 绥远当局支付此前从蒙古税款中扣除的200,000.00美元，作为百灵庙“蒙古自治政治委员会”的清算费用，以及
5) 惩处所有卷入百灵庙保安队叛乱的相关人员。
傅作义将军拒绝考虑这些要求，结果德王收到来自南京的电报，谴责其公开反叛。
预期的攻击于11月5日发动。满蒙部队从其出发基地上都出发，向陶林和新河两个掩护平绥铁路线的战略要地进军。11月11日与目标接触。11月15日，入侵者对陶林发动猛烈攻击，但被击退。11月18日，中国军队成功发起

page_data.en:
- 8 -
counter-attack against the troops of WANG YING in the region
of Hungerhertu and dislodged them from their positions. The
Mongolian troops then concentrated themselves at Pailingmiao
with the object of attacking Kuyuan and Wuchuan, to the north
of Kweihwa. The Suiyuan troops did not allow themselves to
be taken by surprise and on November 23 they launched a sharp
attack against Pailingmiao and occupied it on the morning of
November 24, compelling their adversaries to retreat to the
edge of the province.
After his defeat at Pailingmiao, Prince TEH, according to
the Chinese information and press agencies, suffered from a
diplomatic illness. He was going, they said, to surrender to
the Government troops. He did nothing. Indeed, under Japan-
ese pressure, his troops, supported by those of his allies,
launched a counter-offensive against Pailingmiao on November 30.
This counter-offensive was brought to a halt on December
4 by the Government troops, who pushed on towards the East. The
invaders retreated to Tamiao located some 100 kilometres to the
north-east of Pailingmiao and their made there new base of
operations. On December 7, the Chinese troops occupied Wulan-
hwa, near Tamiao and on the 10th. at 11 a.m. Tamio was taken.
One entire division (7th) of Prince TEH was annihilated. Sev-
eral commanders of WANG YING's troops surrendered themselves,
including SHIH YU SHAN (石玉山), cavalry commander on the 8th.
and CHIN HSIEN CHANG (秦憲章), infantry brigade commander on
the 9th.
The victory of the Chinese troops seems greatly due to
these defections, provoked by the customary tactics of General
CHIANG KAI SHEK. Indeed, enticing sums of money were offered
to the Mongols and Manchukoans to come over to the Chinese side.
(This information was published in a "Central News" telegram of
November 26.) A general could receive as much as $60,000.00,
whilst a group of soldiers could obtain as much as $5,000.00
if they brought with them a field gun or an anti-aircraft quick-
firer.
page_data.zh:
- 8 -
在昂格尔图（Hungerhertu，音译）地区对王英部队发动反击，并将其从阵地驱逐。随后，蒙古军队集结于百灵庙，意图进攻归化以北的固阳和武川。绥远军队未让对手得逞，于11月23日对百灵庙发起猛烈攻击，并于11月24日上午将其占领，迫使敌军撤退至省界边缘。

据中国情报机构和通讯社消息，德王在百灵庙战败后，称病不出。他们称，他打算向政府军投降。但他并未采取任何行动。事实上，在日本人的压力下，其部队在同盟军的支持下，于11月30日对百灵庙发动了反攻。

这次反攻于12月4日被政府军遏制，政府军随即向东推进。入侵者撤退至位于百灵庙东北约100公里处的塔庙（Tamiao，音译），并在那里建立了新的作战基地。12月7日，中国军队占领了塔庙附近的乌兰花（Wulanhwa，音译），并于10日上午11时攻占塔庙。德王的一个整编师（第7师）被歼灭。王英部队的数名指挥官投降，其中包括骑兵指挥官石玉山（SHIH YU SHAN）于8日投降，步兵旅长秦宪章（CHIN HSIEN CHANG）于9日投降。

中国军队的胜利似乎很大程度上归功于这些叛变，这是蒋介石将军惯用战术所引发的。事实上，中方提供诱人的金钱收买蒙古人和满洲国人倒戈。（此信息刊登于11月26日的“中央通讯社”电报中。）一名将军可获得高达60,000.00美元，而如果一个士兵小组携带一门野战炮或一门高射速高射炮投诚，则可获得高达5,000.00美元。

TRANSLATION OF FRENCH POLICE REPORTS DATED OCTOBER 31, 1936.
（印：SECRET）

SUBJECT: Troop movements during period from 20-9-36
to 20-10-36.

REFERENCE: National Defence.
Disposition of Chinese Troops.

As a result of the settlement of the Kwantung-Kwangsi problem,
the Japanese menace in the Shanghai region and the concentration of
Japanese-Manchukuo troops on the Charhar-Suiyuam frontier, the
National Military Commission has been obliged to proceed with the
regrouping of troops in order to concentrate them in the regions
most menaced.
During the period September 20 - October 20, the following
movements of troops have been made:

1) Nanking troops evacuate Kwantung.

The eight Nanking Divisions (1st, 4th, 6th, 10th, 11th, 14th,
93rd and 98th) which, during August, were transferred to Kwantung,
have evacuated this province and have now been transferred to the
following districts:

1st. Division. - East Kansu.
4th, 6th, 10th & 14th. - Peking-Hankow Rly. Zone.
11th. - Nanking
93rd. - Chekiang
98th. - Kiukiang

2) Concentration of troops in the Shanghai-Nanking-Hangchow region.

In addition to our reports 1201/2 of 6-10-36 and 1352/S of
20-10-36, during the period under review, ten divisions (11th, 36th,
43rd, 49th, 55th, 60th, 78th, 88th, 90th, and the newly formed 20th)
and 4 independant brigades (34th, 35th, 38th and 11th) have reinforced
the troops stationed in this region. Of this total:

Six divisions (36th, 43rd, 55th, 60th, 78th, and 20th) and 3
brigades (34th, 38th and 11th) were transferred from Kiangsi.

One division (90th) and one brigade (34th) transferred from Che-
kiang.

One division (43rd) transferred from Fukien.

One division (88th) from Hupeh and

One division (11th) from Kwangtung (see above)

3) Concentration of troops in the Peking-Hankow Railway Zone.

Prior to October 1, 1936 the following troops were stationed in
the Peking-Hankow Railway Zone:

Eleven Infantry Divisions (25th, 32nd, 33rd, 39th, 41st, 82nd, 91st,
116th, 117th, 141st and 142nd).

One independant brigade (40th).

One independant artillery brigade (2nd).

One division (5th) and two brigades (13th and 14th) of cavalry -
about 110,000 men.

1936年10月31日法国警察报告译文。
（印：秘密）

主题：1936年9月20日至10月20日期间的部队调动。

参考：国防。
中国军队部署。

鉴于两广问题的解决、日本在上海地区的威胁以及日满军队在察哈尔-绥远边境的集结，国民政府军事委员会不得不重新整编部队，以便将其集中在受威胁最严重的地区。

在9月20日至10月20日期间，发生了以下部队调动：

1) 南京部队撤离广东。

8月在广东集结的八个南京师（第1、4、6、10、11、14、93和98师）已撤离该省，目前已被调往以下地区：

第1师 - 甘肃东部。
第4、6、10和14师 - 平汉铁路区域。
第11师 - 南京
第93师 - 浙江
第98师 - 九江

2) 上海-南京-杭州地区的部队集结。

除我们1936年10月6日的1201/2号报告和1936年10月20日的1352/S号报告外，在审查期间，十个师（第11、36、43、49、55、60、78、88、90师以及新组建的第20师）和4个独立旅（第34、35、38和11旅）增援了驻扎在该地区的部队。在此总数中：

六个师（第36、43、55、60、78和20师）和3个旅（第34、38和11旅）从江西调入。

一个师（第90师）和一个旅（第34旅）从浙江调入。

一个师（第43师）从福建调入。

一个师（第88师）从湖北调入，以及

一个师（第11师）从广东调入（见上文）

3) 平汉铁路区域的部队集结。

1936年10月1日之前，以下部队驻扎在平汉铁路区域：

十一个步兵师（第25、32、33、39、41、82、91、116、117、141和142师）。

一个独立旅（第40旅）。

一个独立炮兵旅（第2旅）。

一个师（第5师）和两个旅（第13和14旅）的骑兵 - 约110,000人。

page_data.en:
2

During the course of the first fortnight of October, the following
units have been transferred to this region:

Thirteen infantry divisions (4th,6th,10,13th,14th,21st, 34th,
44th, 47th, 51st,59th,96th, and 129th)

Five independant brigades (3rd,21st,22nd,43rd, and 44th).

One independant artillery regiment (26th) and

Three cavalry brigades (2nd, 3rd and 15th), which makes the
present strength of the troops in this area as follows:

24 infantry divisions.

5 independant brigades.

1 brigade and 1 regiment of independant artillery.

1 division and 5 brigades of cavalry - a total of about
260,000 men (see 1).

Of the units transferred to this district:

Three divisions (2,47,129) and 2 brigdes (3,21 and 22) came from
Hupeh,
Three divisions (51,59 and 96) from Hunan,

Two divisions (13 and 21) from Kweichow,

Four divisions (4,6,10 and 14) from Kwangtung,

One division (4) and two brigades (43 and 44) from Shansi.

4) Reinforcement of troops in Suiyuan.

During the period September 20 - October 20, three infantryt
divisions (70,71 and 72) and one cavalry division (2nd) have been
transferred to Suiyuan, in order to reinforce the provincial troops.
Of this number:

Two divisions (70 and 72) came from Shansi and one division (72)
from Shensi.

----------

Other transfers include:

1st. Army HQS (General Hu Tsung Nan) transferred from Kwangtung
to Kansu.
28th. Army HQS (GenLIU CHIEN HSU) from Hunan to Changsha.
19th. Army HQS (Gen. WANG TSING KUO) from Western Shansi to Suiyuan.
7th. Division HQS (Gen. TSING FAN TSUNG) from Northern Shensi to
Suiyuan Kansu.
28th. Division HQS (Gen. Tung Tsao) from Northern Hupeh to Changtu.
1st. Cavalry Brigade HQS (Gen. Chang Chao Tang) from Northern
Shensi to Tienshui (Kansu).
1st. Artillery Brigade HQS (Gen. Hse Wen Kwei) from Northern
Shensi to Tienshui (Kansu).

十三个步兵师（第4、6、10、13、14、21、34、44、47、51、59、96和129师）

五个独立旅（第3、21、22、43和44旅）。

一个独立炮兵团（第26团）和

三个骑兵旅（第2、3和15旅），这使得该地区目前的兵力如下：

24个步兵师。

5个独立旅。

1个独立炮兵旅和1个独立炮兵团。

1个骑兵师和5个骑兵旅 - 总计约260,000人（见1）。

在调往该地区的单位中：

一个师（第4师）和两个旅（第43和44旅）来自山西。

4) 绥远部队的增援。

在9月20日至10月20日期间，三个步兵师（第70、71和72师）和一个骑兵师（第2师）被调往绥远，以增援省防部队。其中：

两个师（第70和72师）来自山西，一个师（第72师，原文如此，疑为笔误，前文已列72师）来自陕西。

SECRET
Translation of French Report dated October 20, 1936

Concentration of Chinese troops in Soochow-Nanking and
Hangchow-Kashing-Sungkiang areas.

Following the strained relationship between China and Japan,
the Commission of National Military Affairs (General Chiang Kai
Shek) has reinforced the troops stationed in the Soochow-Nanking
and Hangchow-Kashing-Sungkiang areas..

A/ Soochow-Nanking area

Before September 20 the following troops were stationed in
this region :

1) The 87th Division (General WANG KING KIU - 王敬玖 ), the units
of which were distributed between Kiangying and Changshu.

2) Four regiments of the Kiangsu Peace Preservation Corps, quartered
in the Chingkiang area.

3) The Instructional Division, quartered at Nanking.

4) The 23rd Independent Artillery Regiment, stationed at Nanking.

5) The 8th(?) Liaison Regiment, stationed at Nanking and

6) The 1st Regiment of Engineers, stationed at Nanking.

Between September 22 and October 3, the following units
appears to have been transferred into this region :

11th Division (General KAO LI TSU) (甘勵初)
36th Division (General SUNG CHI LIEN - 宋希濂)
78th Division (General KWEI YUNG TSING - 桂永清)
88th Division (General SHEN YUAN LIANG - 孙元良 )
3rd Independent Artillery Regiment (Colonel LI TE MING - 李德明)
4th Independent Artillery Regt. (Colonel KUNG KING KWEI - 孔慶桂)

Defence works are understood to have been thrown up at Kiating
and Yushan.

At Nanking, the surrounding hills - Tse Ching Shan (紫金山),
Yu Hwa Tai (雨花台), Chi Ming Shi (鸡鸣寺) and Tang Shan, have
been declared fortified zones and the construction of shelters,
artillery platforms etc has been pushed forward. Emplacements for
anti-aircraft guns have been constructed near the walls of the
capital.

B/ Hangchow-Kashing-Sungkiang area

Before September 20, the 57th Division commanded by General
LI SUNG SHAN (李松山 ) was stationed in the Kashing area.

Between September 22 and October 15, the following troops
appear to have been transferred into the Hangchow-Kashing-Sungkiang
area :

Head-quarters of the 4th Army; Commander-in-Chief, General
WU CHI HWEI (吴奇伟).

Headquarters of the 27th army, commanded by General LI YUN
CHI (李云杰).

1936年10月20日法国报告译文

中国军队在苏州-南京和杭州-嘉兴-松江地区的集结。

鉴于中日关系紧张，国民政府军事委员会（蒋介石将军）已加强驻扎在苏州-南京和杭州-嘉兴-松江地区的部队。

A/ 苏州-南京地区

9月20日之前，以下部队驻扎在该地区：

1) 第87师（王敬玖将军），其部队分布在江阴和常熟之间。

2) 江苏保安团的四个团，驻守在镇江地区。

3) 教导总队，驻守南京。

4) 第23独立炮兵团，驻守南京。

5) 第8(?)通信团，驻守南京，以及

6) 工兵第1团，驻守南京。

在9月22日至10月3日期间，以下单位似乎已被调往该地区：

第11师（甘励初将军）
第36师（宋希濂将军）
第78师（桂永清将军）
第88师（孙元良将军，原文英文为SHEN YUAN LIANG，括号内中文为孙元良）
第3独立炮兵团（李德明上校）
第4独立炮兵团（孔庆桂上校）

据悉，嘉定和玉山已构筑防御工事。

在南京，周围的山丘——紫金山、雨花台、鸡鸣寺和汤山——已被宣布为 fortified zones（设防区），掩体、炮台等的建设正在加紧进行。首都城墙附近已修建高射炮阵地。

B/ 杭州-嘉兴-松江地区

9月20日之前，由李松山将军指挥的第57师驻扎在嘉兴地区。

在9月22日至10月15日期间，以下部队似乎已被调往杭州-嘉兴-松江地区：

第4军总部；总司令，吴奇伟将军。

SECRET
Translation of French Report dated October 6, 1936

Concentration of Chinese troops in Soochow-Shanghai area and
Hangchow-Kashing-Sungkiang.

Following the tension between China and Japan, the Commission
of Military Affairs (General Chiang Kai Shek), is reported to
have reinforced the troops stationed in the Soochow-Shanghai and
Hangchow-Kashing-Sungkiang areas.

A/ Soochow-Shanghai Area

Before September 20 the 87th Division of General WANG KING
KIU (王敬玖) was stationed in this area and was distributed as
follows : (I)

Military Headquarters - Kiangyin
259th Brigade.......................Kiangyin
260th Brigade.......................Taitsang-Kiating
261st Brigade.......................Changshu

Between September 22 and 30 the following units appear to have
been transferred into this area :

2nd Division of General KAO LI TSOU (甘勵初)
21st Division of General MMME LI HSI CHOW (李仙洲) (2)
36th Division of General SUNG CHI LIEN (宋希濂)
78th Division of General KWEI YUNG TSING (桂永清)
264th Brigade of the 88th Division of General SHEN YUAN
LIANG (沈元良) (3).

These troops are understood to be distributed as follows :

Kunshan 125th regiment of the 21st Division.
Soochow 126th regiment of the 21st Division.
Wusieh-Ihing 107th and 108th Brigades of the 36th Division.
Changshou Headquarters and 106th Brigade of 36th Division
Chenkiang-Taiyang 264th Brigade of the 88th Division.
Nanking 2nd and 78th Divisions
Nantungchow (North bank of Yangtse) (4)
27th Division of General KAO SHIH HSIUNG (高樹勳)

Defence works are understood to be in course of construction
at Kiating and Yushan.

B/ Hangchow-Kashing-Sungkiang Area

Before September 20 in the Kashing area was stationed the 57th
Division of General LI SUNG SHAN (李松山). The units of this
Division are distributed as follows :

Headquarters ............ Kashing
169th Brigade........... Haining
170th Brigade........... Pinghu
171st Brigade...........Kashing

Between the 22nd and 27th September the following troops
appear to have been transferred into the Hangchow-Kashing-Sungkiang
Area :

Headquarters of the 27th Army of General Li Yun Chi (李雲生)
49th Division of General WU CHIN CHENG (伍誠仁)
58th Division of General YUAN CHAO CHANG (阮肇昌)
